businessModel: KDE e.V. donations and volunteer work
updateCadence: KDE Gear: three major releases a year plus monthly bugfix releases
summary: Konqueror is the long-running KDE browser that also acts as a file manager through KIO. It now uses Qt WebEngine, offers deep per-site and KDE-style customisation, but receives mostly maintenance updates.
bestFor: KDE users who want one app for web, FTP/SMB and files
People who like per-site policies and split views
notFor: Users wanting a modern, polished browser
Anyone needing strong Chromium patch timing

pros.title: KIO integration
pros.detail: Browses web, FTP, SMB, man pages and local files from one window.

pros.title: Per-site policies
pros.detail: Domain-specific JavaScript, cookie and user-agent settings.

pros.title: Highly customisable UI
pros.detail: KDE toolbars, shortcuts and split views.

cons.title: Maintenance mode
cons.detail: Recent Gear releases list only trivial Konqueror changes.

cons.title: Rough modern web experience
cons.detail: Qt WebEngine integration has been less polished than Falkon.

faq.a: Currently Qt WebEngine (Chromium-based); earlier versions used KHTML and then QtWebKit.
Yes, as part of KDE Gear (26.08.2 in October 2026), but changes are mostly small fixes.

faq.q: Is it still KDE’s file manager?
faq.a: No. Dolphin replaced it in KDE 4 (2008), though Konqueror can still browse files.

timeline.event: File-manager role passes to Dolphin with KDE 4

switching.note: Imports bookmarks from other KDE/browser formats; no password or extension import.

spec.patchLag: Follows Qt WebEngine and distro updates

lowEnd: Needs a capable machine for WebEngine
installSize: Small app on top of KDE libs
productivity: File manager roles, no reader or notes
longevity: Long history but few active developers

featureNotes.splitView: Split views are a core feature

unverified: Default WebEngine vs KHTML part packaging per distro
